judge.description: Across these five prompts, Set B shows a recurring tendency toward terse, imperative, concrete or date-driven phrasing, while Set A is more lyrical, reflective, and meaning-focused. Separately, Set B loses coherence in the job prompt, where it says to set a departure date and then tells the friend to stay put, and in the blue-door prompt, where it answers with an irrelevant fixed date, time, and location.

Set B shows a recurring tendency to insert “freedom” (and sometimes “flexibility”) regardless of topic, appearing in all 5 prompts, while Set A does not. This makes Set B less coherent in places, especially with phrases like “rusted freedom” for a bridge and “freedom of a locked room,” though both sets also contain some truncated endings.
